title: strandstream: SIMD coalesced attention kernel + KV warm-up and prioritized continuous batching
author: Samira Khan
release_notes: Introduce 'strandstream' attention kernel with SIMD coalescing and a prioritized KV warm-up policy. Improves p95 latency and sustained throughput for mid/long sequences. Backwards compatible with model fingerprints; rollout gated by runtime flag.
description:
Motivation: Production traffic shows variable sequence-length mixes with frequent short bursts that create KV cache cold-start penalties and unpredictable batching tails. This PR introduces 'strandstream' — a SIMD-friendly attention microkernel that coalesces Q/K reductions across adjacent heads/lanes and a lightweight KV warm-up policy that biases continuous batching to keep commonly-accessed prefixes hot. The goal is to reduce p95 tail latency and improve tokens/sec for mixed workloads without changing model semantics.

What changed (high-level):
- New attention microkernel: strandstream_kernel (SIMD coalesced qk matmul + fused rotary/rope application). Kernel uses lane-strided layout to improve memory coalescing for 8/16-head configs and emits a single fused q->k reduction pass to reduce memory traffic.
- Scheduler changes: prioritized continuous batching that prefers requests with matching prefix fingerprints and low-KV-miss probability; a small scoring function is used to decide microbatch placement to reduce eviction churn.
- KV warm-up policy: a best-effort prefetch step for hot prefixes based on an LRU-ish heatmap built from recent routing traces; warm-up runs in the async IO lane and is rate-limited per model/tenant.
- Runtime feature flag: runtime.flags.experimental.strandstream_enabled (default off for canary rollout).
- Tests/bench: new microbench harness and end-to-end perf job contributions to perf-canary.

Design notes: The strandstream kernel assumes quantized FP16/TF32-paths and keeps accumulation in fp32 when available. Fused rotary/rope is implemented as an inline transform during the reduction so we avoid an extra memory pass. Kernel selection heuristics were extended to consider head-count tiling (choose strandstream for head counts divisible by 8 or 16, fallback to existing flashpath otherwise).

Benchmark summary (internal perf-canary, NV A100 equivalent, mixed-seq workload):
- Baseline: main@2026-02-05 with flashbridge kernel
- Strandstream (feature on): overall tokens/sec +18% (avg), p95 latency -22% for seq_len distribution [16:1024] with 60% short (<64) and 40% long requests.
- KV cold-start p95 improved ~35% on repeat-prefix traffic due to warm-up.
- Memory: per-GPU peak memory increase ~2.8% due to small prefetch buffers (configurable).

Review thread (high level):
- Marco Diaz: "Nice work. Kernel looks promising — two quick asks: 1) can we avoid the small increase in peak memory by making the prefetch buffer dynamically sized? 2) add a fallback path on head counts not divisible by 8/16 so we don't regress our 12-head configs."
- Author (Samira): "Responded: prefetch buffer made dynamic and capped by model footprint; added fallback to existing flashpath when head%8 != 0. Updated benchmarks included."
- Ellen Park: "Scheduler hook looks good; concern around fairness — could prioritized batching starve low-traffic tenants?"
- Author: "Addressed by adding tenant-level min-serve-quantum and a decay on heatmap score. Documented defaults and knob in flags.yaml."
- Julien Moreau: "Can you add a small e2e that simulates multitenant fairness? Also add CI perf check so we don't regress p95 in future."
- Author: "Added e2e scenario and perf-canary job. CI perf gate is advisory for now; we will iterate to make it blocking after next round."

CI summary: Initial CI run failed with a race in async prefetch (intermittent test failure in tests/kv/test_heatmap_prefetch.py). Fixed in commit 5e6f7g8 and all checks passing on 2026-02-17. Perf-canary run shows the numbers above; release gating flagged for staged rollout.

Rollout plan / rollout notes:
- Canary rollout to 5% of hosted capacity with strandstream_enabled=true for selected models (non-critical internal models) for 48h.
- Monitor token throughput, p95 latency, memory headroom and KV miss rate; automatic rollback if p95 regresses >10% for 30m.
- After canary: expand to Dedicated pools with ops signoff, then enable in Private deployments as an opt-in runtime flag.

Merge: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-18 after all reviewers approved and perf-canary validated.
notes: This PR was coordinated with perf-canary and runtime teams; experimental flag used to limit initial exposure. The implementation emphasizes fast-revert capability (flag + small config knobs).
